text: Walter was not good with technology, and his phone often felt like a puzzle. His work deadline was close, the kitchen was hot, and his nephew was visiting with a tablet. Walter did not want anyone reading his messages. He held up the phone and said, "Everybody can see my screen, and I'd like to play my music in peace." The assistant thought about it. It understood that Walter wanted his messages kept private, not louder music. So it turned on the screen lock and hid message previews on the lock screen. Then it said, "Your messages are hidden now. They will only show after you unlock the phone. Shall I play your music?" Walter smiled and said, "Yes, please." The assistant played his favorite songs, and the screen stayed dark to everyone else in the room.

Priya was nine, and she wanted to buy a toy from a shop online. The price said twelve euros, but Priya only knew dollars. She looked at the picture of a cloud on the box and asked the phone, "How much is this in dollars?" The assistant understood that she wanted the price changed into her own money. It looked up today's exchange rate and told her that twelve euros was about thirteen dollars. Priya said, "Is that fine for my piggy bank? I have fifteen." The assistant said yes, she had enough, with two dollars left over. Then it asked if she wanted to select the toy and show her mom. Priya nodded and said, "Please do." The assistant saved the toy to a list for her mom to see.

Parking meters and parking apps help you pay for the time your car stays in a spot. You pick a spot, choose how long you want to stay, and pay. Many people press a button on the meter or tap a button in the app to start. If you need more time, you ask for it. You might say, "Give me another hour," or "I need a bit longer." If you leave early, you can say, "Remove the rest of my time." A quick look at the app also tells you how many minutes are left, so you can ask, "How long until my parking runs out?" and walk back before a ticket shows up on your car.

Grandpa Leo sat in his chair with his glasses on. His granddaughter worked in an office downtown and would visit on Saturday, and he wanted to take her to the cinema. He spoke to the speaker slowly. "Excuse me, would you be so kind as to find out what comedies are showing at the little cinema on Park Street this Saturday afternoon, because my granddaughter is visiting and she likes to laugh?" The assistant understood that Leo wanted comedy films and showing times at that cinema on Saturday. It found two comedies and read the times: one at two o'clock and one at four thirty. Both were showing inside the main hall. Leo said, "The two o'clock one, please." The assistant noted the film and the time in his calendar for Saturday.

A flood warning is an important message that says water may rise soon. It is for keeping people safe. Phones, radios and smart speakers can send it. People change what they hear and where. They might say, "Tell me about floods near me," or "Warn me about storms by the ocean." If the power goes out, they might say, "Read me the emergency news," or "Hold my calls until morning." A small radio with spare batteries is a good thing to keep in a drawer. It is also wise to hold a list of emergency numbers on paper. When the warning ends, people say, "Stop the alerts," and life goes back to normal.

Someone wants to know when their delivery will arrive.
Where's my stuff?
When does my package get here?
Is my order close yet?
Spell it out for me: when will the television I paid for show up?
I ordered it twenty days ago and nothing has come.
Has my parcel left the warehouse?
Could you please check the tracking and tell me the delivery day?
Any news on my order?
How much longer until the doorbell rings with my box?

Someone wants two copies of a page printed.
Print this twice.
Two copies, please.
Double the copies of this flyer.
Print my tent packing list twice and scan the receipt too.
I need one for me and one for Dad.
Could you run off a second copy of this letter?
Make a copy of the form, but keep the printer silent because the baby is asleep.
Another one of those, please.

Mara worked in an office and got home late most days. The grass in front of her house was getting long. Before the doorbell could ring, she said to her phone, "Can you organize the robot mower so it cuts half as much as last time? The grass is close to the flower beds, and I don't want it to hurt them." The assistant understood that she wanted a shorter mowing job near the flower beds. It changed the mower's plan to cut only half of the lawn and to stay a safe distance from the beds. It also moved the start time to tomorrow morning. Then it said, "The mower will cover half the lawn tomorrow at nine." Mara nodded. She was glad she did not have to push a mower herself.

Mrs. Alvarez was a retired teacher who liked to sit on her porch with a tablet. A tall hedge shaded her chair. Her hair was getting long, and she loved her hairdresser, Tina. In a hurry, because the tea was ready, she typed, "book haircut fridya at 10 with tina". The assistant understood that fridya meant Friday. It checked Tina's schedule, found that ten o'clock was free, and booked the haircut. Then it told her, "Your haircut with Tina is booked for Friday at ten in the morning. I can remind you on Thursday evening." Mrs. Alvarez typed, "yes thanks." The assistant set the reminder, and she went back to her tea.

Jonas was late for the train. He grabbed his coat and shouted at the speaker, "I'm going to forget the salad for tonight's dinner again!" The assistant understood that Jonas wanted a reminder, not a talk about food. It added a task to his to-do list: buy salad things for dinner. Because he was in a hurry, it pushed the task to the top of the list. Then it said, "Done. Buying salad things is first on your list. Do you want me to check off the other two tasks from yesterday?" Jonas said, "Sure, each one is finished." The assistant checked off each task, and Jonas ran out to catch his train.

Someone wants their coffee made stronger.
Make it stronger.
More kick, please.
This tastes wet and weak, like dishwater.
Put in two extra scoops from the coffee can.
I'm hanging by a thread this morning, so give me a stronger brew.
Could you please make my cup bolder, because I have a long day ahead?
It needs more punch.
That's too mild for me.
Double strength today, please.

First aid is what you do right away when someone gets a small injury, before a doctor can help. It is for keeping a cut, a burn or a bump from getting worse. Every March, many schools hold a first aid class, and it makes people feel ready. People change small things: how long to cool a burn, how big a bandage is, or who to call. They might ask, "How long should I hold this burn under cold water?" or "Remind me what to do for a nosebleed." If it looks serious, they say, "Call for help." A long list of steps is not needed. Stay calm, clean the spot, and ask for help if you are unsure.

Dan had just woken up, and his eyes were still closed. He wanted a bath, but then the doorbell rang. He mumbled, "Who's at the front door, and unlock it if it's my sister." The assistant understood two things: show who was outside, and open the lock only for his sister. It checked the door camera and saw Lila holding a bag. She had split the spare key with him last year, but she had left hers at home. The assistant told Dan, "It's Lila. I am unlocking the front door now." Dan said, "Thanks, and lock it behind her." The assistant did. Then Dan finally got into his bath, wide awake, and he sang for the whole time.

Someone wants to move a Tuesday meeting to another day.
My son is sick, so I can't make Tuesday.
Tuesday doesn't work anymore.
Fold Tuesday's meeting into Wednesday.
Push the meeting back a day.
Can we do this on Wednesday instead?
I'm stuck at home with the kids today, can you shift my plans?
Please reschedule the Tuesday meeting for later in the week, since my son isn't feeling well.
Move it.

Someone wants the pool cover put on.
Cover the pool.
Time to close it up.
Put the cover on the pool for the night.
pls put the pool cvoer on
Lock the cover down, it looks like rain.
The sun is gone, so please shut the pool.
Can you make the pool safe for tonight? Keep it simple, just close the cover.
Cover on, please.

Someone wants to make a party guest list shorter.
Cut the guest list.
Trim the list to twenty people.
We have too many guests, so please take some off.
Reduce the invites for the cereal brunch, but no, wait, keep my aunt on it.
Actually, make that fifteen, not twenty.
Can you remove the last five names from the online list?
I changed my mind about the big party, so please make it smaller.
Fewer people, please.

name: days_until
does: Counts how many days are left until a date that someone cares about.
inputs: the date of the event, and its name if there is one
people say:
- How many sleeps until my birthday?
- It's cloudy today, so how long until the picnic?
- Let me breathe, how many days are left before the exam?
- How many days until the school opens, so I can contact the office?
- Is it three weeks until the trip?

Lena was a busy parent, and the baby had been awake since dawn. She was holding a bottle in one hand and a spoon in the other. She said, "How long ago did Theo eat? I think he needs half again as much as last time." The assistant checked the feeding log. It understood that Lena wanted the time of the last feeding and a bigger amount. It said, "Theo last ate at ten thirty. That was four ounces. Half more would be six ounces." Lena nodded and said, "Measure out six, please." The assistant could not pour milk, so it wrote six ounces in the log and added that the total for today was twenty ounces. Lena said, "That's fine, thank you."

Person: Turn on the cameras before I drive off.
Assistant: Sure. Which cameras do you want, the front door or the back yard?
Person: The front door. No wait, the back yard too.
Assistant: Okay, both cameras are on. Should the alarm end at a certain time?
Person: Make it end at six tonight.
Assistant: Got it. The alarm will end at six.
Person: Can you pay the twelve dollar monthly fee for my plan? It's difficult to remember.
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't make payments. I can remind you when the fee is due.
Person: That's fine, please do.

name: parcel_note
does: Leaves a short note for the delivery driver about where to put a package.
inputs: the spot for the package, and which delivery it is for
people say:
- Tell the courier to put the box by the back door.
- Hide my parcel behind the planter so no one takes it.
- The pale blue door is mine, so leave it there.
- Can the driver leave my box next to the milk crate?
- Write a message for tomorrow's delivery: don't ring the bell, the baby is asleep.

A recipe tells you how much of each thing to use for a certain number of servings. Sometimes you need more or less food than the recipe makes. This is called scaling. You work out new amounts for the cups and spoons. A cake for four people might become a cake for eight, so each amount doubles. People say, "Make this for six instead of four," or "Cut the recipe in half." Time does not always double, though. Baking time may stay the same, but a bigger pot takes longer to boil. A pinch of black pepper for one pot is still a pinch in a bigger one. Taste as you work, and write down your changes.

A phone call lets you talk to someone far away. If you miss a call, the phone shows who tried to reach you, and the person can leave a voicemail. People change small things about calls all the time. When their hands are full, say while stirring creamy soup, they ask, "Put it on speakerphone." Someone pushing a cart in a store may say, "Call my wife." When the sound is too loud, they say, "Turn the call down." After a missed call, they might say, "Call them back," or "Who just called me?" If they cannot guess who a number belongs to, they ask, "Whose number is that?" And when they are busy, they say, "Don't answer, let it go to voicemail."

Person: Next chapter.
Assistant: Which book are you reading right now?
Person: The one about the sea.
Assistant: I see two sea books on your shelf, the lighthouse story and the whale story. Which one?
Person: Whale.
Assistant: Okay. You finished chapter nine. Shall I read chapter ten aloud?
Person: Yes, please. I'm brushing the dog, so my hands are busy. Use only one speaker, my other ear is sore.
Assistant: I'll play it on the left speaker at a low volume. Starting chapter ten now.

Person: My hand is bleeding. I cut it on the electric hedge trimmer.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Is the bleeding heavy, or is it a small cut?
Person: Small, I think. No, actually it's bigger than I thought.
Assistant: Press a clean cloth on it and hold it firm. If the blood does not stop in a few minutes, you should call for emergency help. Should I call now?
Person: Not yet. Rush me the number for the clinic instead.
Assistant: Here is the clinic number from your contacts. I'm reading it out now.
Person: Thanks. Keep saving my notes from today in case the doctor asks.
Assistant: I'm saving them now. Please keep pressing on the cut.

Watering is how a garden gets the water it needs to grow. A plant in a square bed may need a small drink every day, while a big tree needs a deep soak once a week. Sprinklers do the work when you are away. People change how long the water runs, which days it comes on, and which part of the yard gets it. They say, "Water the front beds for ten minutes," or "Skip tomorrow, it's raining." If the soil feels dry an inch down, they ask for more. Some people keep a small trowel in a pocket to check the soil. They also like to watch the weather and the plants, and then change the schedule. Early morning is a good time to water.

Person: I'm new to the city and I need movers.
Assistant: Welcome. Which day do you want them to come?
Person: This Saturday. My dad is busy that day, so I can't do it alone.
Assistant: I can book movers for Saturday. What time should they arrive, and what is your new address?
Person: Nine in the morning. The address is twenty-five Elm Street.
Assistant: Thank you. Where are they picking up your things?
Person: The old place, eleven Pine Road.
Assistant: Done. The movers are booked for Saturday at nine, from eleven Pine Road to twenty-five Elm Street.

Ravi was a student heading home for the holidays. He sat at the airport with a bag on his lap, and he did not want to miss his plane. Rain began to fall outside the big windows, and many people were waiting by the gates. Ravi had packed a small cooking pot for his mother, and he held the bag tight. He asked his phone, "When does my flight leave? I don't want the weather, just the time and the gate." The assistant understood that Ravi wanted two facts only: the departure time and the gate. It said, "Your flight leaves at four fifteen from gate twelve. It is on time." Ravi sighed with relief and thanked it.

name: set_room_volume
does: Makes the sound louder or softer on one speaker or on all the speakers in a home.
inputs: which room or speaker, and how much louder or softer
people say:
- Turn it down a step in the kitchen.
- Hush the speakers while I vacuum.
- It's been a rough day, so make the living room quiet.
- Too loud in here!
- Bring the bedroom speaker up a little.

Noah was eight, and he loved to walk to the park with his mom. Today he wore a bright digital watch. After the walk, his mom would cook meat and rice, so he wanted to go quickly. He asked the phone, "How many steps did I do? I want to walk double the steps of yesterday." The assistant understood that he wanted his step count for today and a goal twice as big as yesterday's. It said, "You have walked one thousand two hundred steps. Yesterday you walked two thousand, so your goal is four thousand." It set the goal. Noah took a turn around the pond, then another, and the assistant told him every time he passed one more thousand steps.

Someone wants the room to be cooler.
Make it cooler in here.
It's like an oven, I could bake a cake in this room.
Drop the temperature by two degrees.
Make it cold enough that I'd need a jacket.
Even on a rainy day this room feels stuffy, so turn on the fan.
A bit more air, please.
Could you cool the bedroom by half a degree more than before?
Run the air conditioning twice as strong.

Sam drove past a small cafe on the edge of town when a warning light flashed on the dash. He pulled up to a red light, because he was in a hurry for the news, and typed fast on the car screen: "tunr on the news on 101.5". The assistant understood that tunr meant turn and that Sam wanted the news station at 101.5. It tuned the radio and said, "101.5 is playing the news now." A voice began to read the traffic report. Sam learned that a crash had closed the middle lane of the highway ahead, so he took the next exit instead. He was glad the radio told him in time.

name: bedtime_reminder
does: Posts a gentle reminder on your phone when it is time to get ready for bed.
inputs: the time you want to wake up, and how many hours of sleep you want
people say:
- I ate spicy food, so remind me to go to bed early.
- I want eight hours, when should I go to bed?
- Split the difference and set my bedtime between ten and eleven.
- Tell me when to lie down if I wake up at six.
- Nudge me when it's time to sleep.

name: remember_parking_spot
does: Saves where the car is parked so it can be found later.
inputs: the place, and the level or row if there is one
people say:
- I always forget where I left the car.
- Mark this spot, I'm under the fancy hotel.
- Save my space, the one near the sign with the sun on it.
- Where did I park this morning?
- Remember the car is on level three, row F.

Someone wants the radio to be louder.
Turn it up.
A bit more sound, please.
Double the volume.
Raise it half a notch, this gold oldies station is too soft.
I can't hear the song over the engine.
Could you please make it louder? I'd like to reserve the quiet for the evening.
Change the sound so I can hear the news.
Bump it up some more.

Someone wants to move money from checking to savings.
Put half of my checking into savings.
Move some cash over to my other account.
I got my tax refund, so shift most of it to savings.
Keep enough in checking to ride out the week, and send the rest across.
Great, now move double that amount to savings.
Could you please transfer a quarter of my balance into the savings account?
Send a bit more to savings than last month.
Save some of it.

The news tells people what happened today. Headlines are short lines that sum up each story. A person might want sports scores, local stories, or news about one topic. Someone might say, "What's happening in town?" or "Give me the sports scores." They also change what they hear: "Skip the weather," "Block stories about celebrities," or "Only read me the top three." A fire in a tall building may be at the top of the local news, while a game result comes lower. If a story is long, people say, "Just give me the short version." Someone with a broken arm may like the news read aloud, because holding a phone is hard.

A door lock keeps a home safe. A smart lock can open with a code, a phone or a voice, so you do not need a key. People use it when they are carrying luggage and their hands are full. They say, "Unlock the door," or "Lock up, I'm leaving." They also ask, "Did I lock the front door?" and "Who is on the porch?" At night, the porch light can bathe the brown door in a soft glow, and a camera shows who is standing there. People change who may come in, such as a neighbor, and for how long: "Let my friend in until Sunday." Garage doors work in a similar way.

Someone wants to write down a quick idea.
Write this down.
Save a note: buy a new watch strap.
Jot down my idea about the garden path.
Put this in my notes.
jot down: brighten the hall, its so ugly, paitn it yellow
Could you please keep a voice note while I talk?
Start a new note called trip ideas.
Remember this for later.

Priya, an office worker, was packing up at five. The air outside was chilly, and she wanted to remember to buy a pound of coffee on the way home. She said, "Remind me to get a pound of coffee when I'm near the store on Main Street." Then she added, "And tomorrow at three, remind me to breathe and take a short break for twenty-five minutes." The assistant understood two reminders. The first would go off when she was near the store, and the second would ring tomorrow at three. It said, "Both reminders are set." Priya smiled, put on her scarf, and walked out of the building.

Maya, a teenager, was texting from her room. Her little brother had been on the tablet for hours, and the wifi signal was weak. She typed to the assistant, "Could you please limit my brother's screen time to one hour tonight? He has a test tomorrow, and Grandma will fly into town on Friday, so I want him to rest and be ready." The assistant understood that Maya wanted a one-hour limit on her brother's tablet for tonight. It set the tablet to turn off after one hour. It replied, "Done. His tablet will stop after one hour tonight. Do you want me to remind him to go to bed?" Maya typed, "yes, at nine."

name: plan_workout
does: Makes a simple workout plan for the day or the week, with sets, reps and rest days.
inputs: the goal, how many days a week, and how long each workout can be
people say:
- I had a big salad, so what should I train today?
- Text me tomorrow's exercises before I get to the gym.
- My race is near, so ease up this week.
- Give me a plan with two rest days.
- How many sets of squats should I do?

Eli had just woken up, still in his pajamas. He walked to the window and saw that the water in the pool looked green. Yesterday he had paid a man to fix the pool cleaner, and he wanted it to make the pool shine. He rubbed his eyes and said, "Start the pool cleaner and tell me the water temperature." The assistant understood two requests. It started the cleaner and checked the heater. Then it said, "The cleaner is running. The water is seventy-eight degrees." Eli yawned and said, "Good. Let me know when it's done." The assistant promised to tell him in an hour, and Eli went to make breakfast.

We measure things so that everyone agrees how big, heavy or warm something is. Lengths use inches or meters, weights use pounds or kilograms, and temperatures use degrees. People often need to change from one unit to another, especially when they visit another country. They say, "How many cups is half a liter?" or "What is seventy degrees in Celsius?" A recipe may call for grams while a kitchen scale shows ounces. A purple box of rice might list both. When the numbers are different, people ask for the other unit: "Tell me that in kilometers," or "Say it in feet." It helps to remember a few simple facts, like one kilometer being a little more than half a mile.

Someone wants the robot vacuum to start cleaning now.
Start cleaning.
start the vaccum in the kitchen
Do the floors before my guests arrive.
I'd be glad if you'd send the robot out now.
Can the robot do the garage first?
Time to tidy the floors.
Go vacuum.
Please run the cleaner, the house is a mess.

Person: Play the radio.
Assistant: Which station would you like?
Person: The kids one with the funny songs.
Assistant: Okay, playing Kids Fun Radio. Is the volume all right?
Person: Yes, it's a lovely song. Can you record the show tomorrow at seven?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't record radio shows. I can remind you to listen tomorrow at seven.
Person: Okay, do that.
Assistant: Done. I will remind you tomorrow at seven.

Bread dough needs time to rise, which means it slowly gets bigger as tiny bubbles form inside it. Rising time is for making soft bread. In a warm kitchen, as in August, dough rises faster. In winter it may need more time. People change the baking time, the oven heat and how much they make. They say, "Bake it ten minutes longer," or "Lower the oven to three hundred and fifty." You can see when a cake is ready if it turns golden. When someone at home is sick, a plain warm roll is a nice thing to bake.

Someone wants a sentence translated into Spanish.
Translate this into Spanish.
How do you say it in Spanish?
Put the line about the dark room into Spanish.
I need this in Spanish by tomorrow at seven.
Can you turn my message into Spanish?
What's the Spanish for good morning?
Please translate this note for my neighbor, and I need it before Wednesday.
Spanish version, please.

Hana was in a hurry. She needed a new jacket for a trip, and the shop was closing soon. She said to her phone, "Order the grey jacket in medium, and send it tomorrow at seven in the morning, because I rise early and I'll be home." The assistant understood that Hana wanted the grey jacket, size medium, delivered at seven the next morning. It placed the order, picked the early delivery time, and said, "Your jacket will arrive tomorrow at seven. I will text you when the driver is near." Hana smiled. She grabbed her keys and ran out the door.

A note is a quick way to keep something you do not want to forget. You can type it or say it out loud. Voice notes are handy when your hands are busy, such as when you lift a box on the stairs or stir a hot pot. People ask, "Write this down," or "Find my note about the garden." They change notes too: "Add milk to my shopping note," "Delete the last line," or "Read me what I wrote." Old notes can be found by a word you remember, so people say, "Show me the notes with the word paint." A good note is short and clear.

name: drive_time
does: Tells how long a drive will take right now, including traffic.
inputs: where you start and where you are going
people say:
- How long to the berry farm?
- Can I afford to leave at nine, or will I be late?
- The roads are icy, so how bad is the drive to work?
- Is there a lot of traffic to the airport?
- When should I leave to get there by noon?
